transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-18
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Singh (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Cobalt Labs), Mark Reynolds (Infra Lead), Samir Patel (ML Eng)
Recording ID: ff-20270618-cb-03

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, request logs, and debugging flows. Customer interested in Dedicated for production, wants to validate error/regression detection and request-level debugging.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec. This is Lena from Redwood, with Omar on the call, our SE. Priya, Mark, Samir, thanks for taking the time.
[00:12] Priya: Thanks, Lena. Excited to see the tracing stuff, we've been hitting some weird 5xxs in prod and it's been a pain to triage.
[00:18] Omar: Cool, totally. Goal for today is to show tracing, error analysis, request logs, and how you can pivot from a high-level alert down to the single request and prompt that caused it. We'll also show how this ties into Dedicated/VPC setups.
[00:30] Mark: Quick note, we're mostly in GCP, and we need VPC peering options and KMS integration. Also latency targets are 200ms p50 for short prompts.
[00:40] Lena: Great, we'll cover network/KMS notes at the end. Omar, want to share screen?
[00:45] Omar: Yep, sharing now - can everyone see the Redwood Console?
[00:50] Priya: We see it. UI looks familiar.
[00:56] [01:10] Omar: Alright top-left is the tracing view. You can filter by model, route, customer id, or tag. I'm going to filter to their prod route - here you can see a heatmap of latency and a spike this morning around 09:42 UTC.
[01:26] Samir: That spike — is that per-token or end-to-end?
[01:30] Omar: End-to-end request latency. If you click into the spike it opens the trace waterfall with segment times - model inference, KV cache lookup, network, and any middleware.
[01:45] [02:00] Omar: Here's a trace that shows long tail during cache miss. You'll see KV cash - sorry, KV cache - warmup cost and subsequent token generation delay. The console annotates where batching and kernel selection happened.
[02:20] Mark: Sometimes our infra shows high CPU on the host when these occur, could that map to batching?
[02:25] Omar: Yes, batching can increase host CPU briefly. The trace shows batch size and which requests were aggregated. You can set batching thresholds per route to control that.
[02:40] Priya: Can we get raw request logs for the single request?
[02:44] Omar: Yep, switch to the request logs tab. We persist request logs for X days depending on plan, and you can export them. Here's the raw request payload, headers (redacted), the prompt, token counts, model used, and the response.
[03:00] [03:20] Omar: Note: sensitive fields are automatically masked if you enable PII redaction. We also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[03:30] Samir: On the logs, some things look garbled — the transcription of system messages was off in our pipeline, any chance of that?
[03:36] Lena: Are you referring to the transcript output or logs?
[03:38] Samir: The logs, sometimes names or acronyms get mis-typed, e.g., 'V-P-C' vs VPC, or 'KV cash' shows up in some of our earlier debug dumps.
[03:46] Omar: Yeah transcription isn't perfect, and sometimes we inherit label quirks from upstream agents. But you can search by normalized terms and we surface fuzzy matches.
[04:00] [04:15] Omar: Back to trace — here's the error-analysis panel. It aggregates by error class (5xx, model-timeout, decoding errors). You can click an error group to see top failing prompts and relative regression since last rollout.
[04:32] Priya: Regression alerts - is that tied to evals/prompt sets?
[04:36] Omar: Exactly. You can attach a prompt set or eval to a route. If the error rate or quality drops vs baseline we trigger alerts and create a regression report with examples and traces attached.
[04:50] Mark: What's the SLA for alerts — near real-time?
[04:54] Lena: Alerts are near real-time; there is a small aggregation window to avoid noise but you get sub-minute detection for obvious spikes.
[05:05] [05:30] Priya: For compliance, we need audit logs for admin actions. Is that available in the console?
[05:34] Omar: Yes, audit logs for role changes, model rollouts, route changes are available and exportable to your SIEM. We also have SSO/SAML and RBAC controls.
[05:45] Samir: Can we see a quick example of tracing a 5xx error from alert to root cause?
[05:50] Omar: Sure — I'm going to simulate a failing request and then show the flow. Running now... okay, alert popped up. Click the alert, it links to the error group.
[06:10] [06:30] Omar: In the error group you see a stack of affected routes and a link to the top failing prompt. Clicking that opens the request log plus a collapsed trace. Here's the request payload — notice the prompt has an out-of-distribution token causing decoding failure. The trace shows model threw a decoding error at token 12.
[06:50] Priya: Can we set automatic fallback to a safer model variant when decoding errors spike?
[06:54] Omar: Yes, routing policies allow you to fallback to compatible model variants automatically. You can configure thresholds for error-rate-based fallbacks.
[07:10] [07:45] Mark: For Dedicated customers, do traces contain full request bodies or are they scrubbed?
[07:50] Lena: For Dedicated you control retention and scrubbing; defaults mask PII but you can opt into full retention for debugging if compliant with your policies.
[08:05] [08:30] Omar: Now demoing a request-level debug: you can replay the request from the console to a sandbox model to reproduce. That sends the same headers and prompt but marks it as replay and doesn't affect production metrics.
[08:50] Samir: Nice. That would help reproduce flakiness.
[08:55] [09:10] Priya: About KV cache — our infra relies heavily on long context and KV cache hits. How does Redwood surface cache efficiency?
[09:20] Omar: There's a cache-efficiency metric per route. You can see hit/miss rates, and traces show whether the request used a warm cache. Also we surface prefix matches and cache key cardinality.
[09:40] Samir: Any advice for tuning batch window vs latency?
[09:45] Omar: Typical pattern: for low latency SLOs keep max batch size small and use adaptive batching. Redwood Optimize will recommend settings based on observed traffic; we can run a quick analysis during POC.
[10:05] [10:30] Priya: Security: KMS integration details?
[10:34] Omar: We integrate with GCP KMS and customer-managed keys for Dedicated. We also support HSM via our private deployment. I'll attach the KMS integration doc after the call.
[10:50] Mark: How about data residency — we need logs to stay in EU region for GDPR.
[10:56] Lena: You can pin routes and logs to regions; Private deployments give full control on-prem. We'll include this in the SOC2/security doc pack.
[11:15] [11:40] Omar: Switching to the request-logs view again, you can run a free-text query across logs, filter by response code, model, token range, or user id. Here's an example query showing all 5xx in the last 24 hours for route 'prod-chat'.
[11:58] Samir: The query language — is it Elastic-like?
[12:02] Omar: It's similar, supports boolean ops and time windows. You can save queries and wire them to alerts.
[12:15] [12:40] Priya: Any limits on exporting logs? We want S3 exports.
[12:44] Omar: Exports to S3 are supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted plan supports csv/json exports via the console.
[12:58] Mark: About debugging, can we attach traces to GitHub issues or Slack?
[13:04] Omar: Yes we have integrations — Slack alerts with a short link and GitHub issue templates that include a trace permalink and scrubbed payload.
[13:20] [13:50] Samir: If we roll a new model version and see regressions, can we easily compare traces between versions?
[13:56] Omar: You can compare time ranges and pin model versions. The regression report highlights changes in error rate, latency, and top failing prompts per version.
[14:12] Priya: What about cost attribution per trace? We need token-level cost.
[14:18] Lena: Console surfaces token breakdown and estimated cost per request; you can group by team or route. That helps correlate cost spikes with traffic patterns.
[14:35] [15:00] Priya: Any existing customers using Redwood for regulated healthcare?
[15:04] Lena: Yes, a few — we have healthcare customers on Private/Dedicated with strict audit and KMS controls. We'll share redacted case studies.
[15:18] [15:40] Omar: Quick demo of error-analysis quick filter: selecting 'decoding errors' shows top prompts and example traces. Then I click an example and you'll see the replay-to-sandbox button and the 'open in tracing' action.
[15:58] Samir: That replay button — does it re-run with identical runtime kernels?
[16:02] Omar: We try to match kernel selection and quantization profile but there are small differences in timing since sandbox might be a different instance class. We tag replays that differ in kernel selection.
[16:20] [16:45] Priya: For POC we'll want a Dedicated pool for a week to run benchmarks — what's the fastest path?
[16:50] Lena: We can provision a trial Dedicated for benchmarking; I'll kick off the internal request once you sign the go-ahead. Typical lead time 2-5 business days depending on capacity.
[17:05] Mark: Licensing and pricing model for Dedicated?
[17:10] Lena: It's reserved capacity pricing; we'll send a starter estimate. Pricing also includes optional observability retention and premium SLA add-ons.
[17:28] [17:50] Priya: Are there any pitfalls you see from our current notes?
[17:56] Omar: Based on what you said — long contexts and heavy use of KV cache — watch cache key cardinality. If keys are nearly unique you get high miss rates. Also monitor batch size variance; big variance can cause tail latency.
[18:12] Samir: We'll share our sample logs and a representative traffic trace.
[18:16] Lena: Great. We'll use that to run Redwood Optimize and provide batching/quantization suggestions.
[18:28] [18:50] Omar: Now I'm going to show linking traces to alerts in a demo incident timeline. You'll see a sequence of alert -> regression report -> trace -> request log -> replay.
[19:12] Priya: That workflow looks tight. Is the UI customizable? We want a simplified dashboard for our SREs.
[19:18] Omar: Dashboards are configurable per team and you can create a lightweight view that surfaces only top alerts and critical traces.
[19:36] [20:00] Mark: How do we onboard internally — API keys, secrets rotation, and least privilege?
[20:06] Lena: We recommend service accounts per environment, short lived API keys, and RBAC per route. We'll include an onboarding checklist.
[20:20] [20:45] Omar: Quick Q&A: (Priya) can we set retention per route? Yes. (Mark) Can we stream logs to BigQuery? Yes with export connector. (Samir) Do you support prompt redaction? Yes, PII redaction available.
[21:10] [21:40] Priya: Ok recap — main asks from our side: SOC2 docs, KMS integration details, trial Dedicated cluster, and we'll send sample logs.
[21:52] Lena: Perfect. I'll send the SOC2/security pack and the recording. Omar will follow up with the trace examples and some Optimize suggestions.
[22:05] Samir: One small thing — earlier we saw 'KV cash' typos in logs from a demo last month, can you make sure exported logs are normalized?
[22:14] Omar: We'll check normalization rules and share a quick note; also you can apply search synonyms locally.
[22:30] [22:50] Priya: Anything else before we close?
[22:54] Lena: Next steps are in the follow-ups; we'll aim to have the trial provisioned and docs over by Monday.
[23:05] Mark: Thanks, folks.
[23:08] Lena: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

--- End transcript ---

References shared during call: console demo deck (link: https://redwood.com/decks/console-tracing), SOC2 overview doc (link: https://redwood.com/security/soc2), sample trace permalink (internal).

Recorded follow-up log: 2027-06-18 16:10 UTC - Lena uploaded SOC2 deck and sent to Priya. Omar uploaded sample traces and a cache-warmup note.
